random_entry_control.note: Identical exit rules; only the entry is replaced by uniform draws.

predictability.result: RANDOM_WALK at every tested timeframe and horizon

interpretation: The entry signal carries significant selection value: it beats a random entry under identical exit rules by 0.359% per episode at t = 5.36. It is still not enough. The random-entry baseline under the shipped exit policy is -0.390% per episode, so the signal lifts the result to roughly breakeven rather than to profit. Returns themselves are indistinguishable from a random walk at every timeframe tested, so the value is in cross-sectional selection rather than in serial dependence. No positive cost-adjusted edge is established and promotion remains disallowed.
limitations: Random control draws entries uniformly, which is a weaker benchmark than a matched buy-and-hold.
Perpetual funding is not modelled and is material over three years.
Maker execution is not simulated; a resting limit order may not fill on the move it was sized for.
The exit policy's own negative baseline is where the loss sits and has not been re-engineered.
